ops.entry: WHEN tests are refactored to reduce complexity DO compare old and new predicates on contract-invalid values the old test rejected, not just on passing fixtures or case names; a simpler predicate can admit the wrong type, shape, or value.
ops.why: The test split kept the same passing cases but let a truthy non-string reason pass where a string was required. This check applies to ordinary test refactors more often than the displaced meta-gate registry check.

ops.entry: WHEN a diagnostic substring is reserved for one outcome DO put the marker in interpolated inputs on a different outcome and check the emitted text for collisions; searching for literal producers cannot show that dynamic text keeps the marker exclusive.
ops.why: A non-miss reason could acquire the absence marker from an interpolated status or id. This production-side probe complements the existing search for alternate producers and applies more broadly than the displaced injected-carrier severity reminder.

originals.original: WHEN a guard becomes the sole automated detector for a defect class DO check whether anything watches the watcher — is the guard's own function tracked by a meta-gate or self-grading registry, so a future edit that weakens it doesn't go unnoticed.

WHEN rating severity for a finding about an edited carrier injected into every spawn of a persona DO weight the carrier's blast radius, not just this instance's content — correct-today content does not bound future edits through the same unguarded channel.
